Apache-2.0.note: Apache-licensed code may be part of a GPLv3 work.

EPL-1.0.note: The FSF lists the EPL 1.0 as incompatible with the GPL. Paper bundles the same library as a separate jar. See the open questions in LICENSING.md.

GPL-2.0-only WITH Universal-FOSS-excepti.note: GPLv2-only code cannot be combined with GPLv3 code by itself; Oracle's Universal FOSS Exception is meant to allow distributing it together with other open source software. Whether it covers Cubiq's distribution is not confirmed. Paper bundles the same library.

GPL-3.0.note: The license of the server as a whole.

LicenseRef-BungeeCord.note: BungeeCord's license: the BSD 3-Clause License with an additional clause against commercial software hosting services; see the open questions.

MPL-2.0.note: The MPL 2.0 allows distribution under the GPL as a Secondary License (section 3.3), unless the code is marked as incompatible with Secondary Licenses.

com.velocitypowered:velocity-native.note: Velocity is licensed under the GPLv3; its native module has no license of its own. Its native libraries contain libdeflate (MIT) and use the operating system's OpenSSL, which is not bundled.

net.md-5:bungeecord-chat.note: BungeeCord's license, which covers its chat module, is the BSD 3-Clause License with an additional clause: "You may not use the software for commercial software hosting services without written permission from the author." Such a restriction is not part of an open source license, and the GPLv3 does not allow further restrictions. Spigot's and Paper's APIs expose this library, and Paper bundles it as well.

studio.cubiq:cubiq-api.note: Paper's API with Purpur's and Cubiq's changes, distributed under the GPLv3 like the server.
